g.title: info-tag

g.data-description: the drive glyph, lit. ISM table 2 - solid amber if there is a drive error.
the thermometer glyph. Solid amber on a thermal error - ambient out of range, or a fan failure.
the lightning glyph. Solid amber on voltage out of range, a failed PSU or a failed voltage regulator.
the memory glyph. Solid amber on a memory error.
the PCIe glyph. Solid amber when a PCIe card errors.

rect.data-description: the system health and system ID bar, and the button that switches between the two modes: solid blue - on, healthy, ID mode not active; blinking blue - ID mode active; solid amber - fail-safe mode; blinking amber - a fault, check the event log. The codes are the R660's table 129 (dell/control-panel-left-16g@1). NO RATE IS PUBLISHED for either blink, so 1 Hz is this library's reading and is not a figure Dell states.

rect.data-states: off ready transfer updating disabled fail-safe unresponsive
rect.data-description: the iDRAC Quick Sync 2 bar, and the button that turns the feature on and off. Every code in the R660's table 130, at the shape that table gives (dell/control-panel-left-16g@1): off, solid and blinking white, five rapid blinks then off, solid and blinking amber. The 2.5 second tail of `disabled` is this library's reading of 'and then turns off'.

g.data-description: the system cover and the backplane cover on top, and the optional security bezel on the front. The bezel is DRAWN FITTED, as on the R740xd and R660: it is `mounts`, so the viewer takes it off to show the drives, and `for:` names what it covers.
g.title: bezel

path.data-description: the bezel - end plates and honeycomb - over an open ground

circle.data-description: the keylock - unlocked with the bezel key before the bezel comes off (ISM 'Removing the front bezel', step 1).

rect.data-description: the release button on the left end plate - step 2 of removal, pressed before the left end is pulled away.
